page.layout: Running head line "EMBLEMA" centred above the title; page number "126" at top left; full-width title in capitals with second line in italic below; engraving (emblem picture) in the middle of the page; four lines of italic verse below the engraving, centred; a marginal catchword-like note "Solem," at lower right.

p.i: Diuinum ingeniùs est omnibus omnia verbum,
Quamuis sit paucis semita trita viris:
Lux est in tenebris: sanctæ lex prætia vitæ,
Est animæ cibus; & clara lucerna poli.

page.notes: The engraving shows a figure with a horn-like device and a bird on his hand, a candle on a stand, a lit candle in a glass case, an open book labelled "Verbum Dei eternum manet" (split across the book's two pages as "Verbum" / "num" and "Dei æter" / "manet"), a sun with a face above, and a pair of spectacles at right. The verse line 1 and the lower-right word "Solem," are printed as shown; "transsibit" is set in italic with the title's "transfibit" spelling as printed on the scan. Doubtful readings: "ingeniùs" (possibly "ingenius") and "prætia" (possibly "præuia"; the scan reads "prævia"-like), and the word "semita" is clear. Verse line 4 ends with a period-like mark after "poli".
